definition: The quantization scheme inside neural codecs: a hierarchy of codebooks where each level encodes the residual of the previous, yielding coarse-to-fine token streams.
details: The quantization scheme inside neural codecs: a hierarchy of codebooks where each level encodes the residual of the previous, yielding coarse-to-fine token streams. Explains why codec-based TTS generates "semantic first, acoustic detail second."

explainer.lead: Residual vector quantization is the quantization scheme used inside neural codecs, turning audio into coarse-to-fine token streams. It explains why codec-based text-to-speech produces semantic content first and acoustic detail second.

tiers.eli5: Like mixing paint in stages: the first coat gives the rough colour, each later coat adds finer shade, and every stage only fixes what the last one missed.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers stack codebooks so each level encodes the residual of the previous one, then decode coarse tokens before fine ones. A pitfall is expecting fine acoustic detail before the coarse semantic level is in place.
tiers.paperLevel: A hierarchy of codebooks where each level encodes the residual of the previous, yielding coarse-to-fine token streams. The definition states the scheme but not specific codebook sizes or error bounds.

explainer.example: A codec-based TTS system first emits a coarse semantic token stream, then successive acoustic levels that encode the leftover detail.
